item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-12085f50dd06e321","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The UN report, covering 2020 rather than 2023, documented 1,053 conflict-related sexual-violence cases in the DRC: 700 attributed to non-State armed groups, 239 to the armed forces, 76 to the national police, and 38 to other State actors. It also reported that sexual violence continued during military operations and that police committed two cases while enforcing pandemic restrictions.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.7","3B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source concerns 2020 and provides only historical context for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report identifies the government and security forces during Félix Tshisekedi's presidency but does not establish his personal direction of the cited abuses.","limitations":["Historical period predates 2023.","The source reports documented cases and attribution, not the full incidence or final accountability record."]},{"source_id":"SRC-12085f50dd06e321","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In 2020, mobile military courts enabled prosecution and conviction of 103 members of the national armed forces and 28 members of the national police for violations; however, court-ordered reparations had not been paid.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The finding concerns 2020, not 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source describes state institutions and government collaboration but does not attribute the court actions personally to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["Historical period predates 2023.","The source does not establish whether reparations were later paid."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0cdf200dce2ccd2d","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In 2023, UNFPA-supported facilities enabled more than 31,000 women to deliver safely at more than 24 health facilities, while three mobile clinics served displaced populations; one mobile clinic recorded about four deliveries per day and no maternal deaths since its February 2023 launch.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly reports 2023 service delivery, though the program was implemented by UNFPA and partners.","ruler_attribution":"The source does not establish that Tshisekedi personally funded, directed, or implemented these services.","limitations":["Attribution is primarily to UNFPA-supported facilities and partners.","The figures are service outputs, not national-level welfare outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0cdf200dce2ccd2d","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Across North Kivu, South Kivu, and Ituri, 5.5 million people were displaced and an estimated 220,000 were pregnant; more than 313,000 women and girls were expected to be at risk in 2023, while UNFPA's appeal to scale services was only 16% funded.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.3","6B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 humanitarian crisis.","ruler_attribution":"The figures describe conditions and international humanitarian funding; they do not by themselves attribute responsibility or policy choice to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["Risk and displacement estimates are not direct measures of presidential action.","The appeal funding level does not identify the government's contribution."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a92c562fb4a93943","start_unit":13,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"On August 30, 2023, Congolese security forces shot and killed dozens of protesters in Goma, wounded scores, and arrested several dozen people after authorities banned the demonstration. Human Rights Watch authenticated videos of soldiers from an elite unit moving bodies onto a truck.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns a 2023 event.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to Congolese security forces and the authorities; the source does not prove Tshisekedi personally ordered the shootings.","limitations":["Casualty totals are described as dozens and scores rather than exact figures.","The source is a human-rights organization account and reports credible evidence, not a final judicial finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a92c562fb4a93943","start_unit":14,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that military authorities had used the state of siege, described as martial law, in North Kivu for two years to crack down on fundamental liberties.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the security-governance context in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the practice to military authorities during Tshisekedi's presidency but does not establish his personal operational decisions.","limitations":["The statement is an organizational assessment rather than a court finding.","It does not quantify all affected persons or specify every implementing authority."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a821c91a1144a6c","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"The DRC revised its 1996 press law in April 2023. The revision introduced a bad-faith clause concerning false information or allegations disturbing public order, did not explicitly abolish prison sentences for press offenses, and guaranteed access to non-classified information of public interest subject to state-security and national-defense exclusions.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns legislation enacted in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source establishes a state legislative change during Tshisekedi's presidency but does not specify his personal authorship or vote.","limitations":["The source does not report implementation, enforcement, or judicial interpretation of the revised law."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2a821c91a1144a6c","start_unit":12,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"RSF reported that the national broadcaster lacked independence; politicians, local authorities, militias, and religious groups pressured journalists; journalists faced arrests, threats, disappearances, and attacks; and security forces were involved in many abuses with impunity. In North Kivu, journalists faced harassment and reprisals from early 2023, while wartime criticism of the armed forces was punishable by death.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The country assessment is presented for 2023 and includes developments during that year.","ruler_attribution":"The source describes state and non-state actors and does not establish that Tshisekedi personally directed each abuse.","limitations":["The assessment aggregates multiple actors and regions.","It does not provide a quantified national total for each abuse type."]},{"source_id":"SRC-dacd52a8fc66890c","start_unit":17,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"UNJHRO documented 5,273 human-rights violations and abuses across the DRC in 2023, averaging 439 per month; this was a 12% decrease from 2022. In the five conflict-affected provinces, documented violations fell from 5,091 in 2022 to 4,473 in 2023.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.6","3B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers January through December 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The figures concern conditions during Tshisekedi's presidency but do not establish personal causation; the decline may also reflect conflict and reporting conditions.","limitations":["Documented violations are not necessarily the total number of violations.","The source does not disaggregate state and non-state responsibility in the extracted passage."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6ef7b5f2572163af","start_unit":16,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"On November 21, 2023, the Congolese government and MONUSCO co-signed a plan for the accelerated, gradual, orderly, and responsible withdrawal of MONUSCO, including a plan and timeline for complete disengagement.","question_ids":["2B.7","2B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns a formal decision in November 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The agreement was signed by the foreign minister and the UN mission head; the source does not state that Tshisekedi personally signed or directed it.","limitations":["The source reports adoption of the plan, not its completion or security consequences.","It does not establish whether the withdrawal improved or worsened civilian protection."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6132630146fc3fd3","start_unit":20,"end_unit":21,"fact_summary":"On January 5, 2023, DRC authorities detained Shilo FM editor Sylvain Kiomba and reporter Joseph Ebondo in Lubao after questioning them about a broadcast alleging secret illegal intelligence holding cells; both were released unconditionally on January 7.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns a January 2023 event.","ruler_attribution":"The detentions are attributed to authorities and the National Intelligence Agency; the source does not establish Tshisekedi's personal involvement.","limitations":["The allegations about secret jails were not adjudicated in the source.","The source does not identify who ordered or reviewed the detentions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-03f984691699d0cc","start_unit":20,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"Journalist Stanis Bujakera was arrested on September 8, 2023, charged with spreading falsehoods, forgery, use of forged documents, and distributing false documents, placed in pretrial detention on September 11, and transferred to Makala prison on September 14. The charges related to a report about possible military-intelligence involvement in the murder of Chérubin Okende, although the report did not name Bujakera as author and the outlet said he did not write it.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Authorities prosecuted and detained the journalist; the source does not show that Tshisekedi ordered the case.","limitations":["The source reports allegations and procedural actions, not a final judgment.","The underlying report's factual accuracy was not resolved in the extracted material."]},{"source_id":"SRC-03f984691699d0cc","start_unit":21,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"President Félix Tshisekedi said on September 19, 2023, that he would not intervene in Bujakera's case, citing separation of powers between the justice system and executive branch.","question_ids":["4B.4","7B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns a public presidential statement in September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The statement is explicitly attributed to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The statement does not establish judicial independence in practice or the fairness of the prosecution.","Non-intervention may represent respect for separation of powers, but the source does not show whether the case was later corrected or remedied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8cd9bd5706687479","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Opposition leaders and former prime minister Bruno Tshibala reported that police repression of the May 20, 2023 opposition march was condemnable, while opponents alleged multiplying rights violations, restrictions on freedoms, and authoritarian drift under Tshisekedi; the authorities had not yet publicly responded in the reported account.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns political events in May 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The allegations concern Tshisekedi's government but are reported as statements by opposition figures and a former prime minister, not as an independent adjudication.","limitations":["The source does not provide an official casualty or arrest account.","The article records allegations and political criticism rather than establishing presidential orders."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1aefb4e3427741a9","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"In March 2023, fighting between M23 and the FARDC intensified and spread from Rutshuru to Masisi, causing hundreds of thousands of people to flee toward Goma; humanitarian estimates placed the displaced population in Goma at more than 300,000, straining food, water, health-care, and other essential services.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.10","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","6B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 conflict and humanitarian crisis.","ruler_attribution":"The source describes fighting by M23 and FARDC and resulting conditions but does not establish Tshisekedi's responsibility for specific military decisions.","limitations":["The displacement estimate is humanitarian and may not be a complete census.","The source does not assess the legality or proportionality of particular FARDC operations."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-5ade8d7d4dddaf39","SRC-41f6559226a57974"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied documents contain little direct evidence about nuclear risk, corruption, macroeconomic policy, appointments, or the ruler's personal integrity.","Several sources report institutional or actor-level conduct during Tshisekedi's presidency without establishing personal presidential authorization or control.","The World Bank page mainly reports indicators for years outside 2023 and does not provide a concrete ruler-linked fact for the supplied lenses.","The UN PSC Framework project page describes activities beginning in 2024 and continuing in 2025, outside the requested 2023 period."]}
